questions.text: Honey is listed as an ingredient, but the pack says Certified Vegan. What should change?
questions.why: Honey is an animal-derived product and cannot be included in vegan-certified foods.

questions.text: Honey is listed as 9% in one file and 1% in another. Which percentage should appear on pack?
questions.why: The honey percentage varies between 9% and 1% across product documents.

questions.text: The pack claims No Added Sugar with 0g added sugars, but lists honey and coconut sugar. What should change?
questions.why: Nutritive sweeteners like honey, coconut sugar, and cane sugar contradict the No Added Sugar claim and 0g declaration.

answers.label: Keep No Added Sugar and 0g added sugars
Keep honey, coconut sugar, and cane sugar

questions.text: Calories are listed as 166, but 15 g fat, 15 g carbohydrate, and 34 g protein give about 331. Which should we use?
questions.why: Printed calories are 166, but 15 g fat, 15 g carbohydrate and 34 g protein calculate to about 331 calories.

questions.text: The pack states May Contain Almonds and Pecans, but both are recipe ingredients. What should be shown?
questions.why: Almonds and pecans are intentional recipe ingredients that must be declared as present, not merely as may contain risks.

answers.label: Keep May Contain advisory for tree nuts
Declare almonds and pecans as ingredients

questions.text: One list has 13 ingredients while another has 16 ingredients including walnuts. Which list should be used?
questions.why: The ingredient lists differ, with walnuts, flax seeds, dried strawberries, and pumpkin seeds only in the 16-item list.

questions.text: Total Fat shows 2.2% Daily Value, but 15 g against 78 g is about 19.2%. Which Daily Value is correct?
questions.why: The label displays 2.2% Daily Value for 15 g Total Fat, but the calculated daily value is about 19.2%.

questions.text: Serving size is printed as 85 with no unit, but 480g over 8 servings gives 60 g. What should be printed?
questions.why: The serving size is printed as 85 without units, whereas dividing 480g by 8 servings yields 60 g.

questions.text: EU-style nutrition icons like kJ and Salt appear on a US pack. Which format should be used?
questions.why: EU-style nutrition wording and reference-intake icons conflict with US nutrition panel requirements.

questions.text: Net quantity is declared as 480g, but ounces are missing. What ounce declaration should be added?
questions.why: US regulations require net quantity in ounces first, but only 480g is specified in the documents.
